title: The Work Package places the payment-matching decision and its record in rwb-decision, while DP-03 keeps the record write in the owning service's transaction and DP-04 keeps the evaluation there, so no source fixes where a match record becomes central
source: Work Package B2-P7-022 story line (service rwb-decision, patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19, secondary true); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and DP-04; RWB-E2-008 sections 4, 12 and 13; RWB-P8-E2008-APP section 1; Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 and its notes through the P7 context pack
description: The Work Package fixes rwb-decision as the service of this slice of RWB-E2-008 and includes DP-03 and DP-04, so the slice holds the rule set and the decision record of the match. RWB-P8-E2008-APP, written from the same key, states that rwb-payment evaluates package PAYMENT_MATCH in its own worker, writes one local decision record per match and per missed payment in its own transaction through the local library and publishes DecisionRecorded, and the P7 CON story lists the package, its rows, its version and the decision log entry as rwb-decision's. The sources give the shape of the record but not the boundary between a record written locally and a record sealed centrally, nor which of the two services answers the in-force version and the dry run.
evidence: Work Package B2-P7-022 story line (legacy RWB-E2-008, service rwb-decision, secondary true, acs []); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 ('Local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1') and DP-04 ('Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision'); RWB-E2-008 section 4 steps 4, 5 and 7 and section 12 (RuleEvaluator in process, ProceedsMatched and PaymentMissed published by P8); RWB-P8-E2008-APP section 1 (the evaluation and the local record are this service's) and section 13 (recordAndApply); RWB-P8-E2008-CON section 19 (the package, its version, its approval, its rollback and the decision log entry belong to RWB-P7-E2008-APP); Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 notes through the P7 context pack ('written by the owning service in its own schema ... then collected into the central ledger in rwb-decision ... JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00').
owner_role: Solution architect, with the decision service owner and the payment service owner
proposed: Keep the Work Package placement and split the record in two halves: rwb-payment writes the local record in its own transaction and publishes it; rwb-decision holds the package, its rows and its test cases, collects the records, appends them to the central hash-chained ledger and runs JOB-14, and evaluates no payment, writes no proceeds row and moves no plan state.

title: No source names the target operations, the DecisionRecorded payload, the decision code of a missed payment, the inputs reference, the parameter key of the input age limit or the read page
source: RWB-E2-008 sections 4, 11, 12 and 14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1, A2.3 and VR-P7-001-3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11
description: The legacy story gives Java signatures and two monolith endpoints, not REST contracts, and no source enumerates the target names or payloads for the record a match writes, the consumer group and dedupe key of the shared topic, the decision code a missed payment carries beyond the D5 code of a match, the physical shape of inputs_ref and of the actions payload, the parameter key of the input age limit of VR-P7-001-3, the default page and size of the decision-log read, or the text of the problem body of a refused record. Those values stand as the placeholder, and the shapes are carried as the legacy interfaces and the TSD fields restated.
evidence: RWB-E2-008 section 12 (RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded, TreatmentApi.runningPlans and recordInstallmentPaid, BatchStatusQuery.forSource; GET /api/recovery/v1/proceeds); section 11 (v_ace_payment, v_ace_account, v_ace_batch_status, proceeds, rule_row and decision_log_entry fields); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry columns), T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT; LOV-DECISION is named but not listed) and T-A.2 API-P7-006 (query caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size); FSD P7 v3 VR-P7-001-3 and A2.3 (the seven field groups of an entry).
owner_role: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-payment, rwb-access and rwb-case
proposed: Fix one DecisionRecorded shape and one consumer group, take the decision codes from LOV-DECISION, carry inputs_ref as an opaque reference to the payment facts of the business date, keep the parameter key of the input age limit as a placeholder read through DP-06, and publish the page default with the read so a consumer never guesses it.

title: The dry-run answer of a rule-package version beyond testResult and dryRunCounts, and whether a caller may supply boundary cases, is in no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 AC-P7-007-01; RWB-E2-008 sections 3 and 7; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; P7 context pack ownership rows (GET /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run)
description: The ownership map gives the dry-run path to P7 and the FSD records the dry-run count in the check set of a version load, but no source describes the answer of the dry run of an existing version, whether it returns the per-test-case result, or whether a caller may pass its own boundary cases. This story needs the two boundary cases of the legacy window to prove that the boundary is row data, and fixes them as cases of the version's own test-case set rather than as caller input.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-007-01 ('50 of 50 test cases passed and the dry run count'); RWB-E2-008 section 3 (package PAYMENT_MATCH version PM-2026.12 with one EXACT row: tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before and 0 after, grace 0 days) and section 7 AC7 (PAY-90004 at 10 days matched, PAY-90005 at 11 days unmatched); P7 context pack ownership rows REST operations provided (GET /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rule registry owner
proposed: Publish the dry run as a read-only operation that returns testResult with total, passed, failed and the failing case IDs, the per-test-case expected and actual result, and the recorded dry-run counts, and keep the boundary cases in the version's own rule_test_case set so the answer is reproducible.

title: The twelve patterns add eight platform build dependencies and four consumed contracts that the metadata rows of a secondary slice do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.4; P7 context pack ownership rows; Work Package B2-P7-022 story line (H [], C [RWB-P8-E2008-CON], I [], X [])
description: The patterns the Work Package fixes add the H rows RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the C rows RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON, while the story line fixes Depends on (build) empty and RWB-P8-E2008-CON as the only contract dependency. The metadata rows are written exactly as the Work Package fixes them and the added rows are carried in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-04 (H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON), DP-06 (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-09 (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), DP-10 (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), DP-15 (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and R5.4; the Work Package fixes H [], C [RWB-P8-E2008-CON], I [], X [] and marks the slice secondary.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the delivery lead
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the Work Package fixes them, name every added row in the pattern table and the fakes of 12.8, build against the published contracts and fakes from Day 1, and let step D1 decide whether the eight H rows and the four consumed contracts enter the dependency map.

title: The name of the rwb-decision database login is in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules
description: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and no document states the login name, its role name or its credential scope, so the story uses the phrase 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and registers the value as missing.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R4 (one login per service) and R5.5 DP-02 (recovery_svc login becomes one login per service); P7 context pack 'Naming and shared platform rules' names the schema, the base, the topic, the queue and the Java package, and no login.
proposed: Let the ACE team allocate the login with the schema rwb_decision and record it in the platform secret store; the story keeps the phrase until it is allocated.

title: A secondary slice with an empty acceptance-criteria list owns no legacy criterion while its ten legacy test cases are kept, and the legacy levels have no counterpart in the template
source: Work Package B2-P7-022 story line (secondary true, acs []); Template and Rules v1 R5.7, R7.2 s7 and s16; RWB-E2-008 sections 7 and 16
description: The story line fixes acs empty, so the nine legacy criteria of RWB-E2-008 belong to the slices that own the payment facts, the match, the treatment plan and the screens, while the ten legacy test case IDs are carried in tcs_legacy and kept. The Covers column therefore names this slice's new criteria and the rules they prove, and the mapping from the legacy System and Access levels to the levels of R7.2 is a ruling of this story.
evidence: Work Package B2-P7-022 story line (acs [], tcs_legacy TC-E2-008-01 to TC-E2-008-10); RWB-E2-008 section 7 (AC1 to AC9) and section 16 (ten test cases, Level System and Access); Template and Rules v1 R5.7 rule 2 and R7.2 s16; RWB-P8-E2008-APP section 16, which keeps five of the same IDs.
proposed: Keep the ten legacy test case IDs in the order the Work Package fixes with the Covers column naming this slice's criteria and the decision-side evidence they give, map System to Component and Access to Contract, and leave the legacy criteria with the slices that own them and with RWB-ITG-E2008-ITG.
